packet.headline_seed: RAF jet carrying defence secretary has signal jammed near Russian border
packet.description_seed: Pilots on board had to use a different navigation system while the plane's GPS was disabled.

what: RAF jet carrying defence secretary has signal jammed near Russian border

clean_source_blocks.text: Russia suspected of obstructing signal on flight bringing John Healey home from visit to British troops in Estonia An RAF jet carrying the defence secretary, John Healey, had its signal jammed for the entire three-hour flight after it flew near the Russian border. Healey had been visiting British soldiers in Estonia and was travelling back to the UK when the electronic attack happened, the Times reported. It is thought Russia was behind the incident on Thursday. Smartphones and laptops were unable to connect to the internet and pilots had to use a different navigation system as the plane’s GPS was disabled. It is unclear if Healey was deliberately targeted but the flight path was visible on aircraft tracking websites. Passengers, who included photographers and a reporter, were told the Dassault Falcon 900LX aircraft could still operate safely.

An RAF jet with the UK defence secretary on board had its signal jammed as it flew near the Russian border earlier this week. John Healey was travelling back to the UK on Thursday after visiting British soldiers in Estonia when the incident happened, the Times first reported. Russia is believed to be behind the attack, which meant pilots had to use a different navigation system as the plane's GPS was disabled during the three-hour flight. The incident took place a day after it emerged that two Russian warplanes had "repeatedly and dangerously" intercepted an RAF spy plane over the Black Sea last month. It is not known if Healey was purposely targeted, but the newspaper reported that the flight's path was visible on aircraft tracking websites. The Ministry of Defence has been contacted for comment.

During his visit to Estonia, Healey spoke to UK service members taking part in a Nato military exercise near the Russian border. In the separate incident last month, a Russian Su-35 fighter approached a Rivet Joint surveillance aircraft, getting close enough to trigger its emergency systems, disabling its autopilot. And a Su-27 jet also carried out six passes in front of the RAF plane, getting as close as six metres (19ft) from its nose. Healey had praised the "outstanding professionalism" of the RAF crew during "unacceptable" Russian flybys, which the MoD said was the most dangerous Russian action since 2022, when a "rogue" pilot fired a missile at a Rivet Joint over the Black Sea. In 2024, an RAF plane carrying then-Defence Secretary Grant Shapps had its GPS signal jammed while flying close to Russian territory. ---
Pilots on board had to use a different navigation system while the plane's GPS was disabled.

Russia suspected of obstructing signal on flight bringing John Healey home from visit to British troops in Estonia

An RAF jet carrying the defence secretary, John Healey, had its signal jammed for the entire three-hour flight after it flew near the Russian border.

Healey had been visiting British soldiers in Estonia and was travelling back to the UK when the electronic attack happened, the Times reported.

It is thought Russia was behind the incident on Thursday.

Smartphones and laptops were unable to connect to the internet and pilots had to use a different navigation system as the plane’s GPS was disabled.

It is unclear if Healey was deliberately targeted but the flight path was visible on aircraft tracking websites.

Passengers, who included photographers and a reporter, were told the Dassault Falcon 900LX aircraft could still operate safely.

Healey had met the Estonian minister of defence, Hanno Pevkur, in Tallinn to discuss long-term bilateral defence cooperation and its strategic expansion.

On Wednesday the Ministry of Defence (MoD) revealed two Russian jets had “repeatedly and dangerously” intercepted an RAF spy plane above the Black Sea last month.

A Russian Su-35 jet flew so close to the British reconnaissance aircraft that it triggered its emergency systems, including disabling the autopilot.

A Russian Su-27 also flew six metres from the unarmed Rivet Joint’s nose and carried out six passes in front.

The MoD said it was the most dangerous Russian action against a British Rivet Joint aircraft since a plane fired a missile over the Black Sea in 2022.

A Rivet Joint is a spy plane, with a crew of up to 30, capable of a wide range of electronic surveillance at a ranges of about 150 miles, and would have been monitoring Russian activity as part of a Nato patrol.

In March 2024, an RAF plane carrying the then-defence secretary Grant Shapps had its GPS signal jammed while flying near Russian territory.

The satellite signal was interfered with for about 30 minutes while the flight was heading back to the UK from Poland.

payload.title: Britannian puolustusministeriä kuljettaneen RAF-koneen signaalia häirittiin Venäjän rajan lähellä
payload.summary: Britannian puolustusministeri John Healey oli palaamassa Virosta, kun häntä kuljettaneen RAF-koneen GPS-yhteys häiriintyi kolmen tunnin lennon aikana. Venäjää pidetään mahdollisena tekijänä, mutta kohdistamista Healeyyn ei ole vahvistettu.
payload.content:
Britannian puolustusministeri John Healey oli matkalla takaisin Britanniaan Virosta, kun häntä kuljettaneen RAF:n koneen signaalia häirittiin Venäjän rajan läheisyydessä. GPS-yhteyden kerrotaan olleen poissa käytöstä kolmen tunnin lennon ajan, minkä vuoksi lentäjät käyttivät muuta navigointijärjestelmää. Venäjän epäillään olleen tapauksen taustalla, mutta ei ole tiedossa, oliko Healey nimenomainen kohde.

## GPS-yhteys poikki lennon aikana

Healey oli vieraillut Virossa brittisotilaiden luona ja tavannut Naton sotaharjoitukseen osallistuneita palveluksessa olevia joukkoja lähellä Venäjän rajaa. Paluulennolla käytetty kone oli Dassault Falcon 900LX, jonka matkustajiin kuului myös median edustajia.

Häirintä vaikutti koneessa olleiden laitteiden yhteyksiin: älypuhelimet ja kannettavat tietokoneet eivät päässeet internetiin. Lentäjät joutuivat turvautumaan vaihtoehtoiseen navigointiin, koska GPS ei ollut käytettävissä. Matkustajille kerrottiin kuitenkin, että kone pystyi jatkamaan toimintaansa turvallisesti.

Tapausta pidetään sähköisenä häirintänä, mutta julkisten tietojen perusteella ei ole vahvistettu, että isku olisi kohdistettu juuri puolustusministeriin. Lentoreitti oli nähtävissä lentojen seurantapalveluissa, mikä on voinut tehdä koneen sijainnista avoimesti seurattavan.

## Taustalla jännitteitä RAF:n ja Venäjän välillä

Tapaus tuli esiin pian sen jälkeen, kun kerrottiin erillisestä vaarallisesta kohtaamisesta Mustanmeren alueella. Viime kuussa kaksi venäläistä sotilaskonetta lähestyi RAF:n tiedustelukonetta. Su-35-hävittäjän kerrottiin tulleen niin lähelle, että tiedustelukoneen hätäjärjestelmät aktivoituivat ja autopilotti kytkeytyi pois päältä. Lisäksi Su-27-hävittäjän kerrottiin lentäneen useita kertoja RAF-koneen edestä, lähimmillään noin kuuden metrin päästä sen nokasta.

Britannian puolustusministeriö on kuvannut kyseisiä ylilentoja vakaviksi ja vaarallisiksi. Healey on aiemmin kiittänyt RAF:n miehistöä ammattimaisesta toiminnasta näissä tilanteissa.

GPS-häirintä ei ole Britannian puolustusjohdolle uusi ilmiö. Vuonna 2024 RAF:n kone, jossa matkusti silloinen puolustusministeri Grant Shapps, koki GPS-signaalin häirintää lentäessään lähellä Venäjän aluetta. Uusin tapaus lisää huolta elektronisen häirinnän käytöstä alueilla, joilla Naton ja Venäjän välinen jännite on jo valmiiksi korkea.
